cases.purpose: Deadline reset-on-fork is carried in sched_setattr flags and read back on an owned process; invalid updates preserve the attributes.
cases.oracle: util-linux 2.41 chrt run by the reference bash side as uid 0 on an owned sleeping Python process; sched_getattr is called directly through the Linux system call (x86-64 number 315) by an independent Python helper.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of the set status, the system-call read-back, the /proc/PID/sched policy/priority/deadline lines and the two rejection statuses and diagnostics.
cases.script:
P=$PWD
cat > "$P/dl.py" <<'X'
import ctypes, os, sys
pid = int(sys.argv[1])
libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
buf = ctypes.create_string_buffer(56)
r = libc.syscall(315, pid, buf, 56, 0)      # sched_getattr, x86-64
if r != 0:
    print('sched_getattr errno', ctypes.get_errno()); sys.exit(1)
size, policy, flags = ctypes.c_uint32.from_buffer(buf, 0).value, ctypes.c_uint32.from_buffer(buf, 4).value, ctypes.c_uint64.from_buffer(buf, 8).value
runtime, deadline, period = (ctypes.c_uint64.from_buffer(buf, o).value for o in (24, 32, 40))
print('policy=%d flags=%d runtime=%d deadline=%d period=%d' % (policy, flags, runtime, deadline, period))
X
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import time; time.sleep(25)' & pid=$!
out=$(chrt -d -R -T 5000000 -D 10000000 -P 16666666 -p 0 $pid 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "set rc=$rc out=[${out//$pid/PID}]"
/usr/bin/python3 "$P/dl.py" $pid
while IFS= read -r l; do case $l in 'policy '*|'prio '*) set -f; echo "proc-sched $l" | /usr/bin/tr -s ' ';; esac; done < /proc/$pid/sched
out=$(chrt -d -T 5000000 -D 4000000 -P 16666666 -p 0 $pid 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "runtime>deadline rc=$rc out=[${out//$pid/PID}]"
out=$(chrt -d -T 5000000 -D 20000000 -P 10000000 -p 0 $pid 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "deadline>period rc=$rc out=[${out//$pid/PID}]"
/usr/bin/python3 "$P/dl.py" $pid
kill $pid; wait $pid 2>/dev/null
echo done
